purpose: Name recurring course forms without overclaiming them as exact disease paths.

course_forms.name: steady decline with clearer terminal phase
course_forms.orientation_value: helps family understand why decline may become visibly cumulative
course_forms.danger: can still miss crises, rallies, hemorrhage, treatment effects, and individual variation

course_forms.name: organ failure with acute crises and partial recoveries
course_forms.orientation_value: explains “better, then worse” and repeated hospital/home cycles
course_forms.danger: can be mistaken for false reassurance after each recovery or false certainty after each crisis

course_forms.name: prolonged dwindling with low reserve
course_forms.danger: can become ageist or obscure treatable distress

course_forms.name: progressive neurodegenerative functional loss
course_forms.orientation_value: keeps communication, swallowing, breathing, mobility, and personhood together
course_forms.danger: can erase agency by equating speech loss with absence

course_forms.name: sudden neurologic crisis
typical_contexts: severe stroke and some catastrophic neurologic injuries
course_forms.orientation_value: explains why palliative care may enter immediately without a long dying phase
course_forms.danger: can be confused with emergency triage or life-support advice

course_forms.name: mixed or unlabeled decline
course_forms.orientation_value: honors bedside truth when the diagnosis label is less explanatory than the decline
course_forms.danger: can conflict with legal cause-of-death vocabulary
